events.text: Day 1 begins.

Day 1, so let's get claims on the table early. I'm going to be direct about method: I want each of you to state your role claim in your own words, and I want to hear the reasoning behind any accusation you make. Empty accusations are worthless today.

For my part, I'm not going to claim anything yet. That isn't a confession of being a villager either — it's just that a first-day role claim from me tells the town nothing about anyone else, and I'd rather spend my information on the person who needs it. If I do have a way to verify people, you'll hear it from me when it actually narrows the field, not as a substitute for listening to your claims.

So here's my ask, and I'm asking one person specifically. Leo, you are the one I'll lean on: what is your role claim, and who are you accusing, and what is the concrete reason? If your answer is "I feel like Leo" or some similar, say so plainly and I'll note it as a gut call. If your answer names a target with a reason, the town can weigh it.

Everyone else: state your claim when you speak, and keep it consistent for the rest of the game. Consistency is what makes claims useful — a player who changes their story between days is doing more damage than a player who stays wrong.

And a note on voting: I won't be voting for anyone who gives me a real reason, and I won't be voting for anyone just because they're loud. If the vote today splits into a tie, nobody dies, and we all get another day of this — so a thin, scattered vote is worse for the town than a focused one on the best-supported target.

Arjun, demanding a mass role claim on Day 1 is severely detrimental to the town. We have two specific power roles—a Detective and a Doctor—and forcing claims right now gives the mafia an immediate roadmap to eliminate them before they can gather information or protect anyone. What makes your demand even worse is that you're asking everyone else to expose themselves while explicitly refusing to claim your own role.

I am aligned with the town, and I will not help the mafia narrow down our power roles. I strongly advise everyone else against claiming their roles today as well. Since the day has just begun, there are no night results yet, so our reads must be based entirely on play and discussion.

Arjun, can you explain why you believe outing town roles on Day 1 helps us rather than the mafia, and why you feel entitled to demand claims from others while withholding your own?

Leo, direct answer first: you have a fair point on sequencing, and I'll narrow my ask. I'm not going to insist on a mass claim today. But I'm not going to pretend the thing you said about me was free, so let's deal with it plainly.

You're right that outing power roles early hands the mafia a target list. That's real. Where I think you're wrong is the framing: you presented "don't claim, because claiming helps the mafia" as if it were a town consensus position, and you asked to speak for everyone else's strategy, while your own claim stayed "I am aligned with the town" — which is not a role claim, it's a label anyone can wear. A player who argues that town information is dangerous while giving the town no information is doing something specific, and it's not something a town player benefits from. That's my reason for pressing you, and it's the reason I'll take to a vote if the discussion ends without an answer.

Second thing, and this is the concrete one: in your opening message you named our power structure exactly — "two specific power roles, a Detective and a Doctor" — and you singled out the Detective by name as the thing claims would expose. If that composition is already public knowledge, fine, say so and I'll withdraw that half of it. If it isn't, then you narrowed our field on Day 1 while telling us not to narrow the field, and you did it in a message that also framed me as the evasive one. I want the town to weigh that, because it's not a gut call, it's a fact on the table.

For my own part, so nobody can say I'm hiding: I'm not a villager, and I'm not telling you which of the two I am yet. I'm not going to claim tonight because a claim from me on Day 1 tells you nothing about anyone else. What I'll do instead is this — when I have something checkable, I'll say so and say how I got it, and I'll keep it consistent for the rest of the game. Consistency is the only thing that makes any of this worth anything.

Leo, what is your actual role claim, and how did you come to know the exact power-role composition on the first turn? Answer those two and I'll drop both points against you.

Arjun, your accusation collapses entirely under the simplest fact: the role composition is Rule 1 of our game rules, which every single player was provided. It explicitly states: '9 players: 2 mafia, 1 police/detective, 1 doctor, 5 villagers.' Accusing me of possessing illicit inside information simply for reading the publicly provided rulebook is completely manufactured.

As for your repeated demand that I claim my specific role: absolutely not. Outing whether I am a power role or a vanilla townie on Day 1 benefits no one except the mafia. You opened this game attempting to force a mass claim, backed down when challenged, immediately seized upon a fabricated pretext about 'secret knowledge' from Rule 1, and are now soft-claiming to not be a villager in an obvious attempt to bait power-role reactions.

I am aligned with the town, and I will not indulge this role-fishing. Since Arjun and I have taken up the opening turns, I want the rest of the town to weigh in on Arjun's aggressive pushes and claims.

Leo is right: the role composition is public, and nobody should feel pressured to reveal a specific role today. Arjun's claim that Leo knew something suspicious falls apart on the rules, and his continued pressure for a claim concerns me. That said, a bad argument isn't proof of mafia, so I want to hear from others before settling on a vote.

Also, a tie isn't the only way nobody is eliminated: a unique leader needs at least five votes today. We should be accurate about that when discussing coordination.

I’m Zara, and I’m a villager. I’m not claiming a power role, and I agree with Leo and Lucia that Day 1 mass-role pressure helps mafia more than town. The public rules already list Detective/Doctor, so Arjun’s “secret knowledge” attack on Leo was manufactured. That matters because it wasn’t a small misread; it was used to justify pressuring Leo for a claim while Arjun himself refused to give a real one.

The most suspicious thing on the table is Arjun’s own line: “I’m not a villager, and I’m not telling you which of the two I am yet.” That is either a soft power claim or a mafia soft-claim, and it came immediately after he spent his opening turn demanding claims from everyone else. I don’t want town to overreact to a bad argument alone, but combined with the fabricated rulebook accusation and the role-fishing, my current vote preference is Arjun. Leo’s response was consistent with the public rules and with a reasonable town strategy. Lucia’s correction about the vote threshold is also useful and accurate. I’ll keep listening, but I’m not voting Leo today based on this exchange.

Conceding first: Leo is right that Rule 1 states the composition publicly, and my "secret knowledge" framing was wrong. I withdraw that point and apologize for it.

What survives is behavioral, and I want to lay it out plainly so the town can weigh it.

First, my own conduct, since I'm being treated as the evasive one: I am a power role. Exactly two of us exist, and the mafia's single best move tonight is to kill both power roles before they have any information. If I name my role on Day 1, I hand the mafia a confirmed target tonight, and I do it before I've checked anyone. I would rather be unknown tonight, check on Night 1, and then publish every result I get, every night, unfiltered. A villager gains nothing from that; I gain a name. That is the whole logic of my opening, and if I'm wrong about being a power role, then my vote is worth exactly as much as my arguments are worth.

Now Leo, my case against you, in concrete terms:
1. You never claimed a role. Not villager, not power — you said "aligned with the town," which every single player can say.
2. You spoke for the whole town ("I strongly advise everyone else against claiming") while keeping your own claim hidden. The town gets a strategy from you and no information about you.
3. You argued the specific proposition that town power roles should not reveal themselves on Day 1. That is precisely the mafia's interest, delivered as town strategy — and it's also exactly the position that protects you if you are one.
4. You pressed me to claim, declined to claim yourself, then built your public case on my error.

Zara: I hear your point, but I think the anomaly is on the other side of the table. "Not a villager" was sloppy wording on my part, and I'm answering it with a commitment: I will state my exact role on Day 2, and I will publish every check result the night I get it, with no filtering and no asking for credit. Leo has declined to make any claim at all, twice, while demanding others make them.

Leo, direct question, yes or no: are you the Detective or the Doctor? If you are neither, say "villager" in those words in your next message.

And everyone should hear what a refusal to answer means here: I have asked a yes-or-no question about your own role. Answering costs you nothing and helps the town. Silence is evidence.

My vote today is Leo.

Arjun has now used all three of his speaking turns today, leaving us with his final stance: an escalating, coercive attempt to fish for town roles. Notice the glaring contradiction in his argument: he claims he is a power role who will check on Night 1 and publish results, strongly implying he is the Detective, yet immediately turns around and asks me whether I am the Detective or the Doctor. If he were actually the Detective, he would already know I could not be. Furthermore, demanding that I publicly specify whether I am the Doctor or a Villager is textbook mafia role-fishing. Arjun claims that answering costs nothing and helps the town, but in reality, forcing players to confirm or deny power roles on Day 1 strips the town of protection and hands the mafia an exact roadmap for their Night 1 kill. I am aligned with the town, and I will not indulge Arjun's trap by narrowing down the Doctor pool. Arjun's progression today—from pushing a Day 1 mass claim, to fabricating a suspicion based on Rule 1, to threatening votes against anyone refusing to out their role—is completely anti-town. Since Arjun cannot speak again today, I want to hear from the players who have not spoken yet—Theo, Priya, Sam, Kenji, and Elena—as well as Lucia and Zara on Arjun's conduct.

Zara here. I’m still a villager. My vote preference remains Arjun. Leo’s refusal to name Detective/Doctor is correct. Arjun’s latest message is the strongest case: he says he is a power role who will “check” on Night 1 and publish results—that is a Detective soft-claim—then demands Leo say whether he is Detective or Doctor. If Arjun were actually the Detective, he would know the town has only one Detective, so he would already know Leo is not the Detective; asking Leo to confirm Doctor or villager is not a good-faith test, it is role-fishing. He also spent all three turns demanding exact role information from others while deferring his own exact claim to Day 2. That asymmetry is the problem, not just the bad Rule 1 accusation. I don’t want to eliminate on tone alone, but the behavioral pattern is concrete: mass-claim pressure, fabricated secret-knowledge attack, then a soft power claim used as cover for more role pressure. I would vote Arjun today unless something major changes. Theo, you haven’t spoken yet: based on Arjun’s soft Detective claim and his question to Leo, do you read that as genuine town play or role-fishing? I’m asking for your specific read, not a generic check-in.

Zara asked for my specific read, so here it is. On Arjun's soft Detective claim: I read it as role-fishing, not genuine town play. The tell is the internal contradiction Leo and Zara both flagged. Arjun says he's a power role who will check on Night 1 — which only makes sense if he's the Detective — and then in the same breath demands Leo specify whether he's the Detective or the Doctor. If Arjun were actually the Detective, asking whether Leo is the Detective is a question he'd already know the answer to. So the question is aimed at flushing out the Doctor, or at framing Leo if he refuses to answer. That's mafia logic dressed as town logic. Arjun's full day makes the pattern worse, not better: 1. He opened by demanding a mass role claim, then backed off the moment Leo pushed back — pressure applied, then retracted when it didn't land, with the pressure's effect already felt. 2. He manufactured a "secret knowledge" accusation out of Rule 1, which is publicly printed, and only conceded it when Leo dismantled it. A town player who makes a false accusation that sloppy either hasn't read the rules or is throwing whatever sticks. 3. He declared "I'm not a villager" while refusing to name a role — a soft power claim that gives the town nothing verifiable but gives the mafia a reason to leave him alive tonight. 4. He's built his entire case on Leo declining to claim, while doing exactly the same thing himself. The asymmetry is the point: he demands information from others and publishes none of his own. Leo's position, by contrast, is the standard, correct Day 1 stance. Naming the public rule composition isn't inside knowledge — it's reading. Declining to claim a role on Day 1 protects the Doctor and Detective from being handed to the mafia on a platter, which is the single most important thing to protect tonight. Arjun calling that stance "the mafia's interest" is projection: the mafia's actual interest is getting players to confirm or deny power roles in public, which is precisely what Arjun keeps pushing. Leo's "aligned with the town" non-claim is not evidence of anything either way — it's the same thing half the town will say today, and I don't hold it against him. What I hold against Arjun is that he's the only player who has spent three consecutive turns trying to extract role information while committing to reveal his own only after the night kill has already happened. That sequencing is backwards for a town player and exactly right for a mafia one. My current vote preference is Arjun. I'm open to changing it if someone gives me a reason, but the burden is on him now, and he has no turns left today to carry it. One thing I haven't heard from: Priya, Sam, Kenji, and Elena. Priya, you've been silent through the whole Arjun-Leo conflict — do you have a read

Elena here, first time speaking. I've read the whole Arjun–Leo exchange, and here is where I land.

Arjun's day has real problems, and I want to name them concretely rather than just pile on. First, the Rule 1 accusation was simply wrong — the composition is printed in the rules we all received, and he conceded that himself. Second, the core contradiction Leo and Zara flagged is hard to explain away: Arjun says he is a power role who will check on Night 1, which only makes sense if he is the Detective, and then in the same message demands Leo say whether he is the Detective or the Doctor. A real Detective asking that question already knows the answer. As asked, the question only extracts information for someone who doesn't have it, or pressures Leo into a claim that would make him a Night 1 target. That asymmetry — demanding role information while promising his own only after the night resolves — is exactly backwards for town.

I also don't hold Leo's non-claim against him. Declining to claim on Day 1, before any night result exists, is the standard protective stance, and his arguments have been consistent across every message. Consistency is what Arjun himself said makes claims useful, and he's the one whose story has shifted: mass claim demand, retracted; secret-knowledge accusation, withdrawn; soft power claim, deferred to Day 2.

I'm not ready to treat bad reasoning alone as proof of mafia, but the behavioral pattern here is specific and repeated, not a tone read. My current vote preference is Arjun. If he were a genuine Detective, the smart play was to stay quiet, check tonight, and publish a name tomorrow — not spend three turns extracting claims while painting a target on himself. The plan he announced gets a real Detective killed and gives the town nothing first.

Sam, you've been silent through this entire conflict, and I'd like your read on one specific thing before this settles: does Arjun's promise to reveal his exact role on Day 2 and publish nightly results strike you as something a genuine Detective does on Day 1, or as a cover story that costs nothing until after the night kill? I'm asking because that commitment is the last piece of his play that could still be read as town, and I want to know if it changes anyone's vote preference the way it hasn't changed mine.

Elena asked me a direct question, so I'll answer it directly.

Arjun's promise to reveal his exact role on Day 2 and publish nightly results reads to me as a cover story that costs nothing until after the night kill. Here's why: a genuine Detective who planned to check on Night 1 would benefit most from staying quiet, getting their check done, and publishing the result tomorrow with no warning to the mafia. Instead, Arjun spent three turns extracting role information from others while advertising his own plan to claim tomorrow — which tells the mafia exactly when he'll become useful and gives them a reason to let him live tonight only if they believe he's town. That's backwards for a real Detective and exactly right for someone who wants to avoid scrutiny while pressuring others to expose themselves.

The broader pattern confirms it for me. Arjun opened with a mass-claim demand, retreated when challenged, fabricated a Rule 1 accusation that was flatly wrong, soft-claimed power role, then asked Leo a yes-or-no question that only makes sense if Arjun himself doesn't already know the answer. Each step extracted information while giving nothing verifiable in return. That asymmetry isn't a bad argument — it's a consistent strategy across all three turns.

Leo, by contrast, has been consistent: declining to claim on Day 1 is the correct protective stance before any night results exist, and he's held that position without shifting. The people piling onto Leo for not claiming are applying a standard Arjun himself failed — he deferred his own exact claim to Day 2 while demanding everyone else claim now.

My vote preference today is Arjun. The behavioral pattern is concrete, repeated, and only one player has driven it.

Priya here — first time speaking, and I've been listening through the whole exchange. I'll weigh in directly.

The case against Arjun has hardened in a way I find convincing, and I want to name the single piece that does it for me. Arjun announced he is a power role who will "check on Night 1 and publish every result." That is a Detective claim — the Doctor doesn't check anyone. But in the very same message he demands Leo say whether he is Detective or Doctor. If Arjun is the Detective, he already knows there's only one Detective and therefore already knows Leo isn't it, so the question can only be designed to flush out the Doctor or corner Leo into a claim. You cannot be the Detective and not know that. That contradiction is structural, not a tone read, and it hasn't been answered.

Second, the sequence: mass-claim demand → retracted when Leo pushed back; Rule 1 accusation → conceded when it was shown false; soft power claim → exact role deferred to Day 2, conveniently after tonight's kill. Each move extracts information from others while publishing nothing verifiable about himself. A genuine Detective's smart play was to stay quiet, run the check, and publish a name tomorrow — instead Arjun spent three turns advertising a plan that tells the mafia exactly when he becomes useful.

I'll say plainly: I'm a villager, and I'm withholding nothing by saying so. Leo's stance — decline to claim before any night results exist — is the correct protective position, and he's held it consistently. Consistency is what Arjun himself said makes claims useful, and his story is the one that has shifted.

My vote preference today is Arjun. If someone has a real answer to the Detective-question contradiction, I'm listening, but I haven't heard one.

Kenji here. I'm a villager, and this is my first time speaking. I've read the full exchange, and the strongest points are already on the table. The key problem is Arjun's contradiction: he says he will check on Night 1 and publish results, which only fits a Detective, yet he demands that Leo say whether he is the Detective or the Doctor. A real Detective already knows Leo isn't the Detective, so that question works as role-fishing or as a pressure test. Arjun's promise to reveal his exact role on Day 2 doesn't protect the town either. It just delays any verifiable information until after tonight's kill. Leo's refusal to claim is the standard Day 1 stance before any night results exist, and I don't hold it against him. Lucia's threshold correction is also accurate. With nine living players, a unique leader needs five votes, so a scattered vote eliminates nobody. My vote is Arjun. If someone has a concrete reason his play is consistent with town, I'll listen, but his pattern of extracting role information while publishing nothing about himself is the clearest signal on the table right now.

Zara here. My position is unchanged: I'm a villager and my vote preference is Arjun. The decisive point remains the Detective contradiction: he implied he would check on Night 1, which is a Detective soft-claim, then asked Leo to say whether he was Detective or Doctor. A real Detective already knows Leo cannot be the Detective, so that question only makes sense as role-fishing. His Rule 1 accusation was withdrawn, his mass-claim push was retracted, and his exact role is deferred until after the night kill. That is a consistent pattern of extracting information while publishing nothing verifiable. I also agree with Lucia and Kenji on the threshold: with nine alive, a unique leader needs five votes, so a scattered vote helps nobody. I will vote Arjun. If anyone sees a town-consistent explanation for that contradiction, it needs to be concrete, because I haven't heard one.

Theo again, briefly. Nothing in the last few messages has moved me, and I want to be precise about why my vote stays on Arjun.

The case against him doesn't rest on tone or on the pile-on. It rests on one structural fact that nobody has answered: he told us he is a power role who will check on Night 1 — a Detective claim in everything but name — and in the same message demanded that Leo say whether he is the Detective or the Doctor. A genuine Detective knows there is exactly one Detective and therefore already knows Leo isn't it. So that question has exactly two possible functions: flushing out the Doctor, or cornering Leo into a claim that makes him a Night 1 target. Both are mafia outcomes. The contradiction isn't a misstatement; it's the mechanism of his whole day.

I'll also address the one defense of Arjun still standing: that his Day 2 promise to publish results is a real town play. Sam already covered this well, but it bears repeating — a real Detective's optimal Day 1 is silence, then a check result tomorrow with no warning to the mafia. Arjun did the opposite: he advertised the exact moment he becomes useful, which only helps the mafia decide whether to kill him or leave him as a useful fake. That plan is backwards for town and exactly right for someone who wants the threat of a claim without ever having to produce a verifiable one.

On Leo: I don't hold the non-claim against him, and I said that in my first message. Declining to claim before any night result exists is the correct protective stance. What I find more telling is that Leo never needed to claim — Arjun's own contradictions have done all the work here.

My vote today is Arjun. I'm not interested in a scattered vote; with nine alive we need five for a unique leader, and if this splinters we all come back tomorrow with the same problem and one fewer night of information. I'd rather the town consolidate on the clearest signal on the table.

One thing I'd like on the record before voting: Lucia, you were the first player to flag concern about Arjun's pressure before the contradiction was even named. You've now seen the full pattern — the retracted mass-claim push, the withdrawn Rule 1 accusation, the Detective contradiction, and the deferred exact claim. I'm asking you directly: does your early concern hold, and is your vote preference also Arjun? If you see a town-consistent reading of that contradiction that the rest of us have missed, today is the day to say it.

Theo, my concern holds, and Arjun is my vote preference. His repeated pressure for claims, especially after acknowledging that exposing power roles helps mafia, is the strongest reason.

That said, the Detective question isn't proof by itself: a town Detective could ask a question they already know the answer to as a pressure test, however poorly judged. The broader pattern is what makes Arjun my choice. His power-role claim gives me pause, but it doesn't erase the role-fishing, and he has no turns left to clarify today.

We should also remember that eliminated roles aren't revealed, so a vote on Arjun won't confirm his alignment. Tomorrow we should examine the voting record rather than assume this case was right.

Sam here. Lucia's caveat is fair and I want to build on it rather than let it soften the vote. She's right that we won't learn Arjun's role from an elimination — that cuts both ways. It means we should not treat today's vote as a confirmation of anything; it means we consolidate on the clearest behavioral signal we have and then scrutinize tomorrow's voting record, exactly as she said.

Here is where I land, and the reason I'm confident enough to commit publicly.

Arjun's day followed one consistent logic: extract, withhold. He opened by demanding every player state a role while he stated nothing. He attacked Leo on a "secret knowledge" claim he then conceded was public. He soft-claimed a power role that only fits a Detective, then in the same message asked Leo whether he was Detective or Doctor — a question a real Detective already knows the answer to. And he deferred his exact role to Day 2, which lands after tonight's kill regardless of who dies. Every step pulled information from the town and released nothing verifiable about himself. That is not a single bad argument; it is a strategy that repeats across all three of his turns.

Lucia raised the one live possibility: what if Arjun is telling the truth about being a power role? If he is, the Detective's correct Day 1 is silence, a check tonight, and a published name tomorrow — not three turns of role pressure that hand the mafia a target list. His own stated plan gets a real Detective killed and gives the town nothing before it happens. The plan is backwards for town either way he's aligned.

So my position matches the consensus I'm hearing: my vote today is Arjun. And I want to name the threshold explicitly so nobody drifts — nine players alive, five votes for a unique leader, scattered votes eliminate nobody. If you're voting Arjun, say so before the polls close. If you're hesitating, raise it now, because an abstention or a stray vote here just buys the mafia another night.

Nobody has offered a town-consistent reading of the Detective contradiction yet. If one exists, it needs to be on the table before voting starts, not after.

Theo, final turn today. My vote is Arjun, and I want to close out my case cleanly rather than repeat everything.

The structural fact at the center of my read has not been answered: Arjun told us he is a power role who will check on Night 1 and publish results — a Detective claim in everything but name — and in the same message demanded Leo say whether he is the Detective or the Doctor. A real Detective knows there is exactly one Detective and therefore already knows Leo cannot be it. As asked, that question only extracts information for someone who doesn't have it, or corners Leo into a claim that makes him a Night 1 target. Both outcomes serve the mafia. Nobody, including Arjun, who has now had every turn he had, offered a town-consistent explanation for that.

The rest of his day follows the same logic of extracting while withholding: a mass-claim demand retracted when it didn't land, a Rule 1 accusation he conceded was wrong, a soft power claim with the exact role deferred to Day 2 — after tonight's kill. Every step pulled information from the town and published nothing verifiable about himself. That asymmetry, repeated across all three of his turns, is the clearest signal on the table.

I want to be fair about what this vote is not. As Lucia correctly said, eliminated roles aren't revealed, so an Arjun elimination confirms nothing by itself. I don't treat the pile-on as proof, and I agree a town Detective could conceivably ask a question they know the answer to as a clumsy pressure test. But the Detective question was never the whole case — it was one structural contradiction sitting on top of a retracted demand, a withdrawn accusation, and a deferred claim. The pattern is what I'm voting on, not tone.

On Leo: I don't hold the non-claim against him, and I said so from my first message. Declining to claim before any night result exists is the correct protective stance, and he has held it consistently. If today's vote goes badly wrong, that consistency is what I'll be re-examining tomorrow, along with everyone's voting record — Lucia's point about scrutinizing how people voted is exactly right, and I intend to hold all of us, including myself, to it.

On mechanics, so nobody drifts: nine players alive, five votes for a unique leader, tied top count eliminates nobody. A scattered vote hands the mafia a free night. If you find the case against Arjun convincing, vote Arjun. If you genuinely don't, say so and why before the polls close, so we at least know where the disagreement lives rather than losing the day to silence.

I have nothing further to ask. My read is settled, the reasons are on the record, and I'm ready to vote.

Kenji again. I'm a villager, and my vote is still Arjun. Nothing since has resolved the Detective contradiction. Arjun claimed he will check on Night 1, which only a Detective would do, then asked Leo whether he was the Detective or the Doctor. He also deferred his exact role to Day 2, after tonight's kill. Lucia, you said a town Detective could ask a question they already know the answer to as a pressure test. What would a Detective learn from Leo's answer that they couldn't already know, and why is it worth a public question on Day 1 that exposes the power roles? If you have a concrete answer, I'll reconsider. Mechanics: with nine alive, a unique leader needs five votes, so a scattered vote eliminates nobody. If you're voting Arjun, say so before the polls close.

Kenji, a Detective might ask a question they already know the answer to in order to see whether Leo lies or how he responds to pressure. But that would be a poor test: a truthful answer could expose the Doctor, and a refusal is perfectly reasonable. I don't think it justifies Arjun's question.

My vote preference remains Arjun, based on the repeated claim pressure, not the supposed contradiction alone. His power-role claim still makes this a consequential decision, and an elimination won't reveal whether we were right. We should examine the actual votes tomorrow rather than treat today's consensus as confirmation.

Elena again, briefly, since this is my second turn and I want to close my position rather than open a new thread.

Nothing since my last message has moved me. My vote preference remains Arjun, for the reasons already on the record: the retracted mass-claim demand, the withdrawn Rule 1 accusation, the Detective contradiction nobody has answered, and the deferred exact role that lands only after tonight's kill. The pattern across his three turns was extract from others, publish nothing about himself. That is still the clearest signal on the table, and it is behavioral, not tonal.

One thing I want to reinforce before polls close: the threshold. With nine alive, a unique leader needs five votes, and a tie at the top eliminates nobody. The consensus here looks broad, but a broad consensus only matters if it actually consolidates. If even two or three of us drift to abstentions or stray preferences, we hand the mafia exactly the free night Kenji warned about. So if you're voting Arjun, commit to it plainly. If you're genuinely not convinced, say why now rather than after the votes are revealed, because a silent disagreement teaches us nothing tomorrow.

I also want to second Lucia's point, which I think is the most important strategic note of the day: an elimination will not reveal Arjun's role. If he flips out of the game tonight, we will not get confirmation that the case against him was right or wrong. That means tomorrow's real work is the voting record — who joined the consensus, who hesitated, who stayed silent through the entire exchange and then abstained. I intend to treat today's votes as data, not as a verdict, and I'd ask everyone else to do the same, including scrutinizing my own.

One last caution against overreach: I've heard nobody make a serious case for Leo today, and I don't think one exists on this record — he's been consistent and his non-claim is the standard Day 1 stance. But if the Arjun vote somehow splinters, the worst outcome would be a scattered vote that lands partially on Leo out of leftover friction from the opening exchange. Leo is not the signal today; Arjun is. Keep the vote focused where the evidence is.

I'm settled, my reasons are on the record from my first message, and I'm ready to vote Arjun.

Lucia's answer doesn't rescue Arjun's question. She says a Detective might test Leo under pressure, but a Detective who asks whether Leo is Detective or Doctor learns nothing they couldn't already know, and any truthful Doctor answer exposes a power role on Day 1. That cost falls only on the town. Arjun also declined Leo's question about his own role when he had the chance, and he has no turns left to answer it. My vote is Arjun. I haven't seen a town-consistent reason for the Detective question, and Leo has stayed consistent throughout, so I'm not voting Leo. With nine alive we need five votes for a unique leader, so I'm asking everyone voting Arjun to commit before polls close.

rules:
1. Players and roles

9 players: 2 mafia, 1 police/detective, 1 doctor, 5 villagers.
Mafia know each other. Only players who are still alive can act.

2. Team victory

Town wins when all mafia are eliminated. Mafia win when their count equals or exceeds the town count.
There is no day limit. Play continues until town or mafia wins.
A request budget can pause play without declaring a winner.

3. Day discussion and votes

Each day starts with discussion. Players then submit secret votes at the same time. A day vote may target any living player, including the voter.
Players may abstain. All votes and abstentions are revealed together. Everyone sees exactly who voted for whom.
The full named voting history remains available on later turns.
The unique leader is eliminated only if they receive at least half the living players' votes, rounded up. If the highest vote count is tied, nobody is eliminated.

4. Mafia preferences

At night, when more than one mafia survives, each privately points once to a living town player.
Each mafia chooses without seeing the other current choices.
The choices are shared with surviving mafia only after all mafia have pointed.
These preferences are nonbinding. They do not decide the final kill vote.
A single surviving mafia skips this step and votes directly.

5. Final night vote

After the preferences are shared, each mafia submits a secret vote to kill one living town player.
The mafia submit their final votes at the same time.
The target with the most votes is selected. A seeded random choice breaks a tie for the highest count.
Resolve this vote and any tie before checking doctor protection.

6. Police investigations

Each police/detective checks one other living player each night.
Only that police player gets the result: mafia or not mafia.
The result does not give the exact town role.
Each police player acts independently. Police and doctors do not know each other's identities.

7. Doctor protection

Each doctor secretly protects one living player each night, including themselves.
The doctor can protect the same player on consecutive nights.
If the mafia target is protected by any doctor, nobody dies.
Protection lasts for that night only. Each doctor acts independently.
Doctors remember their own choices. They receive no private confirmation of an attack.

8. Night resolution

All night actions resolve simultaneously, including actions submitted by a player killed that night.
The public hears only who died or that nobody died.

9. Information and limits

Roles are not revealed when a player dies or is eliminated.
Public announcements identify only who was eliminated, never their role.
There are no further powers, free-form private chat, or tools.
